ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: If $A B=60$ and $D E=48,$ find $C F$
ready1_open_rewrite.title: Geometry3K open-ended problem

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a circle with center C. Segment AB has endpoints A and B on the circle and passes through C, so AB is a diameter. Segment DE is a chord of the circle. Segment CF is drawn from the center C to the chord DE, and the right-angle mark at F shows CF is perpendicular to DE. Reasoning: Given AB = 60, and AB is a diameter, the radius of the circle is 60/2 = 30. Thus CD = 30. Given DE = 48, and the perpendicular from the center of a circle to a chord bisects the chord, DF = FE = 48/2 = 24. In right triangle CDF, CD is the hypotenuse, so by the Pythagorean theorem: CF^2 = CD^2 - DF^2 = 30^2 - 24^2 = 900 - 576 = 324. Therefore CF = 18.

method.method_draft: Use an analytic setup based on the diagram. Read AB as a diameter through center C, so with AB=60 the circle has radius 30. Place C at the origin and orient the chord DE so it is a vertical or horizontal line at distance CF=d from the origin. Since DE=48, its half-length is 24, so an endpoint of the chord has coordinates equivalent to (d,24) or (24,d) depending on orientation. Because the endpoint lies on the circle of radius 30, use d^2+24^2=30^2. Solve to get d=18, and this distance is CF.
